title: Essential: Final Volume
description: Essential Criteria: The student's final answer for the mineral's volume must be approximately 7.8 × 10⁻⁵ m³.

title: Important: Boyle's Law Setup (Initial)
description: Important Criteria: The student must apply Boyle's law to the initial state, relating the initial pressure and volume (p₀, V_B+V_C) to the pressure and volume after valve A is closed (p₀+ρgh₁, V_C).

title: Important: Boyle's Law Setup (Final)
description: Important Criteria: The student must apply Boyle's law to the state with the mineral, relating the initial pressure and volume (p₀, V_B+V_C-V) to the pressure and volume after valve A is closed (p₀+ρgh₂, V_C-V).

title: Important: Correct Variable Definition
description: Important Criteria: The student must correctly define V as the unknown volume of the mineral and subtract it from the appropriate gas volumes in the second setup.

title: Optional: Unit Consistency
description: Optional Criteria: The student demonstrates consistent use of SI units (Pa, m³) or correctly converts all given values.

title: Pitfall: Misapplied Volume Subtraction
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student incorrectly subtracts the mineral's volume V from V_B instead of from the total gas volume or from V_C in the final state.

title: Pitfall: Ignoring Atmospheric Pressure
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student uses only the gauge pressure (ρgh) instead of the absolute pressure (p₀ + ρgh) in Boyle's law equations.
